summary: @servicetitan/hammer-icon preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package presents itself as an SVG icon library but ships a preinstall hook (`scripts.preinstall: node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from GitHub releases, extracts it, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bun, ['math_init.js'], {cwd: D})` to run a sibling 727KB JavaScript bundle. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated in the obfuscator.io / string-array style — hex-named identifiers (`MmgoCP`, `etDiOOB`, `JqTtnbZ`), a >1000-entry rotated numeric/string constants array, and an array-shifting decoder function `WV8StW` — with no legitimate purpose for an icon package. Neither `setup.mjs` nor `math_init.js` appears in the package.json `files` allowlist, which declares only `mdi/{filled,outlined,round,sharp,two-tone}/*.svg` and `CHANGELOG.md`; the loader and payload are shipped outside the author's declared manifest. The alternate-runtime execution path bypasses scanners that inspect only Node-resolved code, and the payload's true behavior is opaque without deobfuscation. Attributes match a dropper pattern targeting the ServiceTitan npm scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
